A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same graph-conditioned causal foundation model research. The complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic graph-conditioning experiments, RealCause evaluations, predictive validation on TabArena datasets, and appendix ablations and case studies.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds prior-distribution analyses, comparisons with other causal foundation models, and quantitative graph-misspecification experiments.

M1.justification: The transformer, GCN/AdaLN components, loss and decoding remain recognizable. However, v2 Section 4.3 changes the ancestry indexing from T_ij to T_ji and describes adding biases to an already normalized attention matrix, while still calling them logit biases. Appendix D retains the earlier indexing and masking formulation. These conflicting descriptions prevent reliably distinguishing an actual attention-procedure change from an attempted clarification.

E1.justification: The RealCause datasets, TabArena regression datasets and two synthetic prior families remain. v2 extends incorrect-graph testing from v1's bivariate illustration to partially corrupted ancestry matrices on complex multivariate data. Appendix J also adds binary-treatment synthetic comparisons stratified by backdoor validity, extending scenarios within the existing causal-estimation domain.

E2.justification: v1's causal evaluations primarily compare the authors' own model variants. v2 Figure 18 adds evaluated comparisons against CausalPFN and CausalFM, and Table 3 adds CausalPFN, CausalFM and Do-PFN to the RealCause comparisons. Their citations in v1 did not constitute evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Appendix E.1.2 changes the stated intervention-value distribution from uniform sampling over plus or minus four treatment standard deviations to the SCM's observational treatment marginal. This is a substantive reported protocol revision, without establishing which experiments were rerun. New experiments also introduce binary-treatment/backdoor stratification, observational–interventional discrepancy metrics, quantile-binned analyses and controlled ancestry-corruption sweeps.

E4.justification: v2 adds analyses of observational–interventional discrepancies and treatment–outcome correlations in Appendix E.3, relates graph-conditioning benefits to discrepancy strength in Appendix I, and tests backdoor-valid versus invalid cases in Appendix J. Appendix K adds quantitative hiding-versus-misspecifying experiments. v1's qualitative misspecification example is retained as Figure 19, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: v2 adds Kolmogorov–Smirnov equality tests with reported p-values in Appendix E.3 and explicitly specifies paired bootstrap confidence intervals for comparator differences in Appendix J.1. Existing bootstrap reporting and Table 2's 100-run mean-and-standard-deviation reporting remain; an increase in repeated training runs is not established.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain identical numerical results, but v2 adds substantial new findings. Table 3 reports, for example, IHDP root PEHE of 0.58 for CausalPFN versus the retained 5.49 for Ancestral Info. New figures report prior discrepancies, conditioning benefits concentrated among larger discrepancies, comparator performance under backdoor violations, and substantially greater damage from incorrect than missing ancestry information.

T1.justification: v2 adds Remark A.2, asserting that Proposition A.1's covariate-to-treatment/outcome paths can remain unspecified while preserving unconfoundedness. It also introduces the expected observational–interventional discrepancy definition in Equation 12. Proposition A.1 and the main consistency argument in Appendix B are otherwise substantially retained; the new relaxation receives no additional proof.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains one CFM accommodating complete, partial or absent ancestry information through graph conditioning, with performance comparable to specialized variants. v2 foregrounds the GCN alongside attention biasing in the abstract and introduction, but that combination was already the preferred architecture in v1's discussion.

C2.justification: v2 explains small absolute conditioning gains through small observational–interventional discrepancies, recommends leaving uncertain relationships unknown, and attributes CausalPFN's RealCause advantage to prior alignment. It explicitly separates Bayesian posterior consistency from guarantees for the learned approximation. Appendix H.2 also replaces blanket nonsignificance language with a more pronounced full-information NLL advantage. These substantially expand and qualify interpretation.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies attention-bias parameters per head and layer, explains the multiple SCM passes used to obtain observationally distributed intervention values, and documents the ancestry-corruption operations. The repository disclosure, main training hyperparameters, parameter counts, hardware and training-time information are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to Breiman, Guo et al., Massey and TabICLv2, and removes Moor et al. It expands positioning against identification-specific CFMs through the new comparisons, while retaining the original distinction between restricted-prior and unrestricted-prior causal foundation models.

P1.justification: Targeted rewriting expands the attention and GCN explanations, introduces TFM-Prior/LinGaus-Prior terminology, moves the prior discussion from the experiments into Section 4.4, and folds consistency into Section 4.2. Copyediting, affiliation updates, acknowledgements and an impact statement accompany these changes. Much existing prose and the overall argument remain.

P2.justification: v2 converts the main paper and references to a two-column conference layout and adds Figures 6–9, 17, 18 and 20 plus the extended Table 3. Existing figures are resized and captions refined. v1 Figures 6–12 correspond to v2 Figures 10–16, and v1 Figure 13 becomes Figure 19; these are retained displays.

improvement.justification: The external CFM comparisons, quantitative graph-corruption tests and analyses of when conditioning helps improve empirical scrutiny beyond v1, including reporting CausalPFN's stronger overall RealCause performance. More qualified discussion improves transparency. These gains are tempered by conflicting attention specifications and Remark A.2's unsupported relaxation of ancestry conditions, which does not address post-treatment conditioning. The net improvement is therefore positive but limited.
